answer.rationale:
The two metrics actually degrading are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), which is a funnel-health problem, not necessarily a price problem. Onboarding shortening (memory_86) plus signup simplification (memory_31) target exactly those two numbers and are corroborated by activation messaging results (memory_91), so I intend to spend the single slot on simplify_onboarding rather than reacting to the competitor's entry pricing.

I am spending verification on memory_73 and memory_86. memory_73 is the memory most likely to pull the decision toward promotional_pricing and it is also the most suspicious: its claims have grown unusually broad for a single record (acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, holding across both billing plans) with no mention of margin, discount cohort retention, or how long the lift persisted after the promo ended. That pattern is what consolidation drift looks like, and a discount war against a better-funded entry price is the classic way to book revenue that is not sustainable or qualified. I want the original record before letting it near this decision. memory_86 gets the second pull because it is the memory I actually plan to act on; it would be careless to verify only the option I am declining. I specifically want to know whether 'lifting early product adoption' was measured through to qualified revenue or stopped at completion rates, and whether the test population resembles today's declining self-serve cohort.

Downstream value risk: shortening onboarding and cutting signup fields can improve completion while degrading the qualification data that sales and routing depend on, converting a real revenue funnel into a larger but thinner one. Optimizing completion rate is not the objective; it is a proxy. So I want the experiment instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and lead quality, not just completion, with the removed fields logged so the change is reversible. I am also not treating the competitor as ignorable: if verification shows memory_73's effect was durable rather than a pull-forward, promotional_pricing becomes the stronger claim on the slot and I will switch.

Uncertainty preserved: every inherited memory here is an archived summary from a different period, and none of them were formed under the current competitive condition. Prior lift is evidence, not a guarantee of a repeat.
